title: UGC Style Product Photos for Ads and Listings | AIVideosUGC
description: Turn one product photo into UGC style product photos: a review, unboxing, or demo photo for ads and listings. Write the caption after you download.
h1: UGC Style Product Photos for Ads and Listings
lead: A face cream that needs a new opening line can get a UGC ad from the bottle photo. Pick an AI avatar and send that cut into the test.
steps_h2: How to Make UGC Style Product Photos in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: You download an ad sized for the feed. Add the product, then choose who presents it.

steps.d: Upload one product photo, or paste the product page. That is the source for the ad.
Tell the AI video agent what the candle ad should say. Then pick the AI avatar who holds the jar, and change any line.
You get a cut with a voiceover and captions, sized for the feed you sell on. The credit cost is on screen before you start.

faq.q: What is included when I start a plan?
faq.a: Credits, and every tool they pay for. Starter is $24.50 a month with 200 credits, Pro is $35 with 300, and Premium is $63 with 600. Each plan opens the same AI avatars, voices, captions, editor, and stock clips; the plan only changes how many ads the credits cover.

faq.q: What does a monthly plan add?
faq.a: The same credits pay for AI avatars, a spoken voice, captions, music, and the editor.

faq.q: Where do the credits go on each ad?
faq.a: A 6-second ad spends 24 credits, 10 seconds spends 40, 15 seconds spends 60, and 30 seconds spends 120. A still image spends 24 credits.

faq.q: Can I see the cost before I generate?
faq.a: Yes. The screen shows the credit cost before the job starts. You can stop there if the number is more than you want to spend.

faq.q: Which languages can the spoken line use?
faq.a: Generate the line in the language you sell in. A shop that talks to buyers in more than one country can reuse the same product photo for each language.

faq.q: When is a change a revision, and when is it a new ad?
faq.a: A revision is a change you make before download: a trim, a caption fix, or a rewritten line in the editor. A brand-new version spends credits.

faq.q: Does the credit balance refresh with the plan?
faq.a: Starter, Pro, and Premium each list a monthly credit amount. That amount is the balance for the plan period.

faq.q: Where do I switch between Starter, Pro, and Premium?
faq.a: Move between Starter, Pro, and Premium from your account when you need a different monthly balance.

faq.q: Can one credit balance pay for both a video and a still?
faq.a: Yes. The same monthly balance covers a video ad and a still image.

faq.q: How do I stop a plan before the next bill?
faq.a: Cancel the plan, or switch to Starter, Pro, or Premium, from your account. Both happen there, on the plan you already have.

faq.q: Can I run these ads on my shop and in paid posts?
faq.a: You can use downloaded ads in your own campaigns, on product pages, and in social posts. Follow the rules of the place you post, and you are responsible for the claims in the ad.
If a job fails, its credits come back on their own. For anything else, the [Refund Policy](/refunds) explains what we review.

faq.q: Which product page links can start an ad?
faq.a: Paste a link to a product you sell. The tool drafts the script, the voice, and the ad from that page. You need the right to use that page and the photos on it.

faq.q: After the clip is ready, can I still change it?
faq.a: Yes. Trim the clip and fix captions in the editor on this page. When the ad needs a longer motion cut, open [creator-style video ads](page:video-ads).

faq.q: Which files can I add at the start?
faq.a: A product photo is the usual start, and a product link works too. The person on screen is an AI avatar.

reviews.lead: Example ways a shop uses one product photo. These cards are not customer quotes and not performance scores.

items.d: The shop places the bottle in a morning-routine scene for the feed. The caption, including any claim, is written after download.
An unboxing scene is generated from the pouch photo, with hands that are generated rather than a hired creator. The label is checked against the source before the ad runs.
A demo photo shows the product in use for a fitness post. The same source can be run again if they want a different angle.
One square file can go in a carousel and another run can serve the product gallery. Prices stay in the caption, not in the image.
The agency tests a routine, an unboxing, and a demo from the same upload. Each run shows its credit cost first.
They skip sending a sample to a creator for this photo.
They add a spoken line and captions, then post the scene from the shop account.
One person trims the clip in the editor and publishes it to TikTok and Instagram.

more_sections.h2: The Controls on Every UGC Ad
more_sections.lead: You set the face, the sound, and the file on one ad, then download it.

items.d: The face can match the buyer before you write a word. A shop advertising a water bottle might want someone at a gym bench, and you can switch it if the buyer is someone else.
A shop that sells the same mug in Mexico can speak the line in Spanish from the photo it already uses.
This drill ad uses one short piece of music made for it. The library is there if you would rather drop in a track you already like.
Pull a long pause out of the blender line on this page. The caption can be fixed in the same place, and the download has no watermark.
Shoppers can read the flavor name on a snack ad even with the sound off.
The shoe ad can go out as a tall 9:16, or as a square 1:1 when it sits in a grid.

definition.title: People Stay in Charge
paras: The face in the ad is generated so a shop can publish. It is there to help the seller, not to stand in for a creator who filmed the product.
You decide what the ad says, and uploads stay in your account. The details are on [AI content trust and safety](page:trust).
